name: שְׁעַרְיָה
gloss: Yah has reckoned; or gate of Yah
summary: Sheariah, one of the six sons of Azel, a Benjamite of the house of Saul through Jonathan, Merib-baal and Micah (1Ch 8:33–38; repeated in 9:44). Scripture says nothing else of him and does not explain the name. It is built like שְׁמַרְיָה Shemariah, “Yah has kept”, a verb with the divine name, which points to the verb שָׁעַר “reckon” (Pro 23:7): “Yah has reckoned”. A noun with the divine name, as עֹבַדְיָה Obadiah his brother is “servant of Yah”, would give “gate of Yah” (compare “the gate of Yahweh”, Psa 118:20); the vowels fit the verb better.

evidence.note: “To Azel were six sons … Azrikam, Bocheru, and Ishmael, and Sheariah (וּשְׁעַרְיָה), and Obadiah, and Hanan.”
The line from Saul and Jonathan down to Azel.
The verb שָׁעַר “reckon”, the likelier source of the name.
“This is the gate of Yahweh (הַשַּׁעַר לַיַהְוֶה)”, for the reading “gate of Yah”.

note: Two readings kept; the verbal one is preferred on the pattern of שְׁמַרְיָה and עֲזַרְיָה. Naming ar-sir records the reckon reading only.
